```{r travelOutcomes, dependson="envOutcome"}

travel_envOutcomes <- full_join(envOutcome_CostSum, fbSieversRoute)
profit_trvl_env <- full_join(AvgProfit, travel_envOutcomes) %>%
  drop_na(n)

travel_HUC12Sum <- travel_envOutcomes %>%
  #group_by(radial) %>%
  group_by(FBndID,HUC12) %>%
  drop_na(Total_Kilometers) %>%
  summarize(AOI = "supplyshed",
            opArea = sum(opArea_ha),
            n       = n(),
            ## Bio yield summary
            BioMg = sum(sum_BioMg),
            
            ## Energy potential summary
            EnergyPot = sum(sumEnergyPot),

            ## Cost summary per field
            DC = sum(sumDC),
            OC = sum(sumOC),
            TC = sum(sumTC),
            DCcp = sum(sumDCcp),
            TCcp = sum(sumTCcp),
            
            ## Wildlife habitat summary
            patch = sum(sum_patch_ha),
            lin = sum(sum_lin_ha),
            prairie = sum(sum_wh_ha),
            rye = sum(sum_rye_ha),

            ## CO2 summary
            CO2 = sum(sumCO2),
            
            ## N2O summary
            N2Ored = sum(sumN2Ored),

            # NO3 load summary
            NO3red = sum(sumNO3red, na.rm = TRUE),

            ## Sediment load summary
            SEDred = sum(sumSEDred, na.rm = TRUE),
            
            Ctruck = sum_BioMg*(2*Total_Kilometers)*0.265, # $ per field. trucking cost. 2026 ISU Custom Rate survey. Transportation coefficient = "haul round bales by truck or trailer per bale per mile", assuming 0.68 Mg of hay in a bale (Hart etal. 2015).
            Ctruck_Mg = (2*Total_Kilometers)*0.265,
            Chand = sum_BioMg*4.7794, # $ per field. 2026 ISU Custom Rate survey. Loading/unloading = "moving large round bales to storage per bale", assuming 0.68 Mg of hay in a bale. Coefficients are assumed to be fixed cost. 
            Ctotal = Ctruck + Chand, # trucking + handling costs per field.
            rnd_dist = 2*Total_Kilometers,
            Ctotal_Mg = (Ctruck + Chand) / sum_BioMg, # transportation cost per Mg of biomass harvested from a field
            Ctotal_Mg_km = Ctotal / sum_BioMg / rnd_dist,
            Cdeliv = Ctotal + sumDC, # cost per field for biomass
            Cdeliv_Mg = Cdeliv / sum_BioMg, # production + transportation cost per Mg delivered from a field
            Cdeliv_Mg_km = Cdeliv / sum_BioMg / rnd_dist,
            Ccpdeliv = Ctotal + sumDCcp, # cost per field for biomass and structural components
            Ccpdeliv_Mg = Ccpdeliv / sum_BioMg,
            Ccpdeliv_Mg_km = Ccpdeliv / sum_BioMg / rnd_dist
            )
```

```{r HUC12_summary, dependson="HUC12_travel"}
huc12_summary <- full_join(Ctravel_HUC12, wsArea)

huc12_summary <- wsArea %>%
  full_join(Ctravel_HUC12) %>%
  full_join(ysHUC12) %>%
  full_join(profitHUC12) %>%
  drop_na(HUC12,sumOPha) %>%
  replace_na(list(sum_UNSTha = 0)) ## 7 HUC12 watersheds had 0 subfields designated as unstable


huc12_df <- huc12_summary %>%
  mutate(
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Landscape-scale metrics
    #
    # The denominator is the portion of each HUC12 within the
    # 32-km supplyshed (`area_ha`), so all outcomes and treatment
    # areas are expressed relative to the same spatial extent.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    per_treated = sumOPha / area_ha,
    per_patch = sumpatch / area_ha,
    per_lin = sumlin / area_ha,
    per_prairie = sumprairie / area_ha,
    per_rye = sumrye / area_ha,

    bio_Mg_ha = sumBioMg / area_ha,
    dccp_ha = sumDCcp / area_ha,
    tccp_ha = sumTCcp / area_ha,

    ghg_ha = (sumCO2 + sumN2Ored) / area_ha,
    no3_ha = sumNO3red / area_ha,
    sed_ha = sumSEDred / area_ha,
    no3_red = sumNO3red/NO3_loadkg,
    sed_red = sumSEDred/sed_loadkg,
    
    
    stabLow_ha = sum_UNSTha / area_ha,
    unprofit_ha = sum_UNPha / area_ha,
    oc_ha = sumOC / area_ha,

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Treatment-level performance metrics
    #
    # These are calculated per hectare treated and are kept
    # separate from the landscape-scale classification.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    no3_per_treated_ha = sumNO3red / sumOPha,
    sed_per_treated_ha = sumSEDred / sumOPha,
    ghg_per_treated_ha = (sumCO2 + sumN2Ored) / sumOPha,
    bio_per_treated_ha = sumBioMg / sumOPha,
    oc_per_treated_ha = sumOC / sumOPha,
    dccp_per_treated_ha = sumDCcp / sumOPha,
    tccp_per_treated_ha = sumTCcp / sumOPha,

    # Treatment composition, not efficiency
    prairie_share_treated = sumprairie / sumOPha,
    rye_share_treated = sumrye / sumOPha
  ) %>%
  filter(sumOPha > 0)

```

```{r multivariate, dependson="HUC12_summary"}
# ============================================================
# MULTIVARIATE HUC12 PLANNING CLASSIFICATION
# ============================================================
#
# The classification identifies recurring combinations of:
#   * conservation/practice configuration,
#   * landscape-scale environmental outcomes,
#   * biomass production, and
#   * treatment extent.
#
# The resulting classes are interpreted as watershed planning
# archetypes within the study landscape. They are not rankings
# and should not be interpreted as universally optimal
# configurations.
#
# PRIMARY ANALYSIS
# ----------------
# K-means clustering is performed on standardized ORIGINAL
# variables.
#
# PCA is used as a diagnostic to:
#   1. describe multivariate structure,
#   2. quantify variance explained,
#   3. visualize variable relationships, and
#   4. provide a sensitivity analysis using PCA scores.
#
# OPPORTUNITY COST
# ----------------
# Opportunity cost is NOT used to define the clusters because
# it is strongly coupled to land-use transformation and prairie
# extent. It is calculated separately and used to characterize
# the economic implementation context of each planning class.
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Prepare HUC12 dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

huc12_planning <- huc12_df


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define PRIMARY classification variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# These variables represent distinct planning dimensions:
#
#   per_treated = extent of landscape transformation
#   per_patch   = prairie patch configuration
#   per_lin     = linear habitat configuration
#   per_rye     = cereal rye configuration
#   no3_ha      = landscape-scale nitrate reduction
#   sed_ha      = landscape-scale sediment reduction
#   ghg_ha      = landscape-scale GHG reduction
#   bio_Mg_ha   = landscape-scale biomass production
#
# Direct cost is retained as an implementation requirement.
#
# Opportunity cost is intentionally excluded from clustering.
#
# IMPORTANT:
# If you decide that direct cost should NOT define the
# archetypes, remove dccp_ha from this vector and from the
# sensitivity analysis below.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

primary_vars <- c(
  "per_treated",
  "per_patch",
  "per_lin",
  "per_rye",
  "no3_ha",
  "sed_ha",
  "ghg_ha",
  "bio_Mg_ha",
  "dccp_ha"
)

cluster_vars <- huc12_planning %>%
  select(all_of(primary_vars))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Retain complete HUC12s
# ------------------------------------------------------------

complete_idx <- complete.cases(cluster_vars)

huc12_cluster <- huc12_planning[complete_idx, ]

cluster_complete <- cluster_vars[complete_idx, ]


# Report sample size explicitly
cat("\nNumber of HUC12s available for classification:",
    nrow(cluster_complete), "\n")

cat("Number excluded because of incomplete classification data:",
    sum(!complete_idx), "\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Standardize variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# All variables are standardized to mean = 0 and SD = 1.
# This prevents variables with larger numerical units from
# dominating Euclidean distance.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cluster_scaled <- scale(cluster_complete)

cluster_scaled_df <- as.data.frame(cluster_scaled)


```

```{r pca, dependson="multivariate"}
# ============================================================
# PCA DIAGNOSTICS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Correlation matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# This is descriptive. It is included to document covariance
# among classification variables, not to claim that the
# variables are statistically independent.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cluster_cor <- cor(
  cluster_complete,
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs"
)

print(round(cluster_cor, 3))

write.csv(
  round(cluster_cor, 3),
  "../data/tidy/archetype_correlation_matrix.csv"
)

write.csv(huc12_planning,"../data/tidy/huc12_clusters.csv"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. PCA
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# PCA is performed on the standardized original variables.
#
# PCA is NOT the primary clustering space.
# It is used to:
#   - describe multivariate structure,
#   - quantify variance explained,
#   - examine variable contributions,
#   - visualize HUC12 relationships.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pca_model <- prcomp(
  cluster_scaled,
  center = FALSE,
  scale. = FALSE
)

pca_summary <- summary(pca_model)

print(pca_summary)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. PCA variance explained
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pca_variance <- tibble(
  PC = paste0("PC", seq_along(pca_model$sdev)),
  eigenvalue = pca_model$sdev^2,
  variance_percent =
    100 * (pca_model$sdev^2 / sum(pca_model$sdev^2)),
  cumulative_percent =
    100 * cumsum(pca_model$sdev^2) /
    sum(pca_model$sdev^2)
)

print(pca_variance)

write.csv(
  pca_variance,
  "../data/tidy/pca_variance_explained.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. PCA loadings
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pca_loadings <- as.data.frame(
  pca_model$rotation
)

pca_loadings$Variable <- rownames(pca_loadings)

pca_loadings <- pca_loadings %>%
```

```{r cluster_analysis, dependson="pca"}
# ============================================================
# NUMBER OF CLUSTERS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Evaluate candidate numbers of classes
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# We evaluate k = 2 through 6.
#
# WSS is an elbow diagnostic.
# Silhouette width evaluates within/between-cluster separation.
#
# Neither metric is used mechanically to select k.
# Cluster size and substantive interpretability are also
# considered.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(123)

k_values <- 2:6

wss_results <- map_dfr(
  k_values,
  function(k) {

    km <- kmeans(
      cluster_scaled,
      centers = k,
      nstart = 100
    )

    tibble(
      k = k,
      tot_withinss = km$tot.withinss
    )
  }
)

print(wss_results)


# WSS plot

ggplot(
  wss_results,
  aes(x = k, y = tot_withinss)
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_values) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Number of planning classes (k)",
    y = "Total within-cluster sum of squares"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Silhouette diagnostics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

distance_matrix <- dist(cluster_scaled)

silhouette_results <- map_dfr(
  k_values,
  function(k) {

    set.seed(123)

    km <- kmeans(
      cluster_scaled,
      centers = k,
      nstart = 100
    )

    sil <- silhouette(
      km$cluster,
      distance_matrix
    )

    tibble(
      k = k,
      mean_silhouette =
        mean(sil[, "sil_width"]),
      median_silhouette =
        median(sil[, "sil_width"]),
      min_silhouette =
        min(sil[, "sil_width"]),
      n_negative =
        sum(sil[, "sil_width"] < 0)
    )
  }
)

print(silhouette_results)

write.csv(
  silhouette_results,
  "../data/tidy/silhouette_diagnostics.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)


ggplot(
  silhouette_results,
  aes(x = k, y = mean_silhouette)
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_values) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Number of planning classes (k)",
    y = "Mean silhouette width"
  )


```

```{r planning_clusters, dependson="cluster_analysis"}
# ============================================================
# PRIMARY FIVE-CLASS SOLUTION
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Fit primary k-means solution
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Five classes are retained for the primary analysis because
# the five-class solution provides an additional meaningful
# distinction in practice configuration while maintaining
# comparable silhouette performance to the four-class solution.
#
# IMPORTANT:
# This is a substantive/model-selection decision, not a claim
# that five is universally optimal.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

k_primary <- 5

set.seed(123)

km_model <- kmeans(
  cluster_scaled,
  centers = k_primary,
  nstart = 100
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Add cluster assignment
# ------------------------------------------------------------

huc12_cluster <- huc12_cluster %>%
  mutate(
    cluster = factor(km_model$cluster)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Cluster sizes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cluster_sizes <- huc12_cluster %>%
  count(cluster, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(
    percent = 100 * n / sum(n)
  )

print(cluster_sizes)

write.csv(
  cluster_sizes,
  "../data/tidy/archetype_cluster_sizes.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Primary clustering diagnostics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

primary_silhouette <- silhouette(
  km_model$cluster,
  distance_matrix
)

primary_silhouette_summary <- tibble(
  k = k_primary,
  mean_silhouette =
    mean(primary_silhouette[, "sil_width"]),
  median_silhouette =
    median(primary_silhouette[, "sil_width"]),
  min_silhouette =
    min(primary_silhouette[, "sil_width"]),
  n_negative =
    sum(primary_silhouette[, "sil_width"] < 0)
)

print(primary_silhouette_summary)

write.csv(
  primary_silhouette_summary,
  "../data/tidy/primary_silhouette_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)


# Silhouette plot for the five-class solution

fviz_silhouette(
  primary_silhouette
)

silhouette_cases <- as.data.frame(primary_silhouette) %>%
  mutate(
    HUC12 = huc12_cluster$HUC12
  ) %>%
  select(
    HUC12,
    assigned_cluster = cluster,
    nearest_cluster = neighbor,
    silhouette_width = sil_width
  ) %>%
  arrange(silhouette_width)

print(silhouette_cases)

silhouette_cases %>%
  filter(silhouette_width < 0)


negative_silhouette_HUC12s <- silhouette_cases %>%
  filter(silhouette_width < 0) %>%
  pull(HUC12)

huc12_cluster %>%
  filter(HUC12 %in% negative_silhouette_HUC12s) %>%
  select(
    HUC12,
    cluster,
    per_treated,
    per_patch,
    per_lin,
    per_rye,
    no3_ha,
    sed_ha,
    ghg_ha,
    bio_Mg_ha,
    dccp_ha,
    oc_ha
  )
```

```{r cluster_sens_analysis, dependson="cluster_analysis"}
# ============================================================
# CLUSTER STABILITY SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Repeated k-means stability analysis
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# K-means solutions can depend on starting values.
#
# We therefore repeat the five-class solution using many
# different random seeds and compare the resulting assignments
# to the primary solution using the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI).
#
# ARI:
#   1.0 = identical partition
#   ~0   = agreement approximately expected by chance
#
# This evaluates stability of the PARTITION, not statistical
# significance of individual variables.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Requires mclust
# install.packages("mclust") if necessary

library(mclust)

set.seed(123)

n_stability_runs <- 500

stability_results <- map_dfr(
  seq_len(n_stability_runs),
  function(i) {

    seed_i <- 1000 + i

    set.seed(seed_i)

    km_i <- kmeans(
      cluster_scaled,
      centers = k_primary,
      nstart = 25
    )

    ari_i <- adjustedRandIndex(
      km_model$cluster,
      km_i$cluster
    )

    tibble(
      run = i,
      seed = seed_i,
      ARI = ari_i
    )
  }
)

print(
  stability_results %>%
    summarise(
      mean_ARI = mean(ARI),
      median_ARI = median(ARI),
      min_ARI = min(ARI),
      max_ARI = max(ARI),
      sd_ARI = sd(ARI)
    )
)

write.csv(
  stability_results,
  "../data/tidy/archetype_stability_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)


# Stability distribution

ggplot(
  stability_results,
  aes(x = ARI)
) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0.8,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Adjusted Rand Index relative to primary solution",
    y = "Number of repeated k-means runs"
  )

# ============================================================
# SENSITIVITY TO NUMBER OF CLASSES
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 16. Compare cluster stability across k
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# This asks whether the selected number of classes is
# particularly unstable relative to nearby alternatives.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(123)

k_stability <- 2:6

k_stability_results <- map_dfr(
  k_stability,
  function(k) {

    # Reference solution
    set.seed(123)

    reference <- kmeans(
      cluster_scaled,
      centers = k,
      nstart = 100
    )

    # Repeated solutions
    ari_values <- map_dbl(
      1:100,
      function(i) {

        set.seed(5000 + i)

        repeat_model <- kmeans(
          cluster_scaled,
          centers = k,
          nstart = 25
        )

        adjustedRandIndex(
          reference$cluster,
          repeat_model$cluster
        )
      }
    )

    tibble(
      k = k,
      mean_ARI = mean(ari_values),
      median_ARI = median(ari_values),
      min_ARI = min(ari_values),
      max_ARI = max(ari_values),
      sd_ARI = sd(ari_values)
    )
  }
)

print(k_stability_results)

write.csv(
  k_stability_results,
  "../data/tidy/k_stability_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# VARIABLE-SET SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. Define alternative classification variable sets
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The primary model contains strongly correlated variables.
# This is not necessarily inappropriate because the variables
# represent different planning dimensions, but it is important
# to determine whether the five-class solution depends heavily
# on particular variables.
#
# Sensitivity sets:
#
# A = Primary model
#
# B = Remove landscape transformation extent
#     (per_treated)
#
# C = Remove highly correlated transformation/biomass variables
#     (per_treated + bio_Mg_ha)
#
# D = Remove direct cost
#
# E = Practice/outcome configuration without direct cost and
#     biomass
#
# These are sensitivity analyses, not alternative "correct"
# models.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

variable_sets <- list(

  Primary = c(
    "per_treated",
    "per_patch",
    "per_lin",
    "per_rye",
    "no3_ha",
    "sed_ha",
    "ghg_ha",
    "bio_Mg_ha",
    "dccp_ha"
  ),

  No_Treatment_Extent = c(
    "per_patch",
    "per_lin",
    "per_rye",
    "no3_ha",
    "sed_ha",
    "ghg_ha",
    "bio_Mg_ha",
    "dccp_ha"
  ),

  No_Treatment_Extent_or_Biomass = c(
    "per_patch",
    "per_lin",
    "per_rye",
    "no3_ha",
    "sed_ha",
    "ghg_ha",
    "dccp_ha"
  ),

  No_Direct_Cost = c(
    "per_treated",
    "per_patch",
    "per_lin",
    "per_rye",
    "no3_ha",
    "sed_ha",
    "ghg_ha",
    "bio_Mg_ha"
  ),

  Configuration_and_Outcome = c(
    "per_patch",
    "per_lin",
    "per_rye",
    "no3_ha",
    "sed_ha",
    "ghg_ha"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 18. Run sensitivity models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

sensitivity_models <- list()

sensitivity_summary <- map_dfr(
  names(variable_sets),
  function(model_name) {

    vars <- variable_sets[[model_name]]

    dat <- huc12_planning %>%
      select(all_of(vars)) %>%
      filter(complete.cases(.))

    scaled_dat <- scale(dat)

    set.seed(123)

    km <- kmeans(
      scaled_dat,
      centers = k_primary,
      nstart = 100
    )

    sil <- silhouette(
      km$cluster,
      dist(scaled_dat)
    )

    # Store model for later comparison
    sensitivity_models[[model_name]] <<- list(
      variables = vars,
      data = dat,
      scaled = scaled_dat,
      model = km
    )

    tibble(
      variable_set = model_name,
      n_variables = length(vars),
      n_HUC12 = nrow(dat),
      mean_silhouette =
        mean(sil[, "sil_width"]),
      median_silhouette =
        median(sil[, "sil_width"]),
      min_silhouette =
        min(sil[, "sil_width"]),
      n_negative =
        sum(sil[, "sil_width"] < 0)
    )
  }
)

print(sensitivity_summary)

write.csv(
  sensitivity_summary,
  "../data/tidy/archetype_variable_sensitivity.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

```

```{r arsi, dependson="planning_clusters"}
# ============================================================
# 19. Compare alternative variable sets with PRIMARY solution
# ============================================================

variable_set_ARI <- map_dfr(
  names(sensitivity_models),
  function(model_name) {

    vars <- sensitivity_models[[model_name]]$variables

    # HUC12s with complete data for this variable set
    sensitivity_data <- huc12_planning %>%
      select(HUC12, all_of(vars)) %>%
      filter(complete.cases(.)) %>%
      arrange(HUC12)

    # Primary classifications for exactly the same HUC12s
    primary_data <- huc12_cluster %>%
      select(HUC12, primary_cluster = cluster) %>%
      filter(HUC12 %in% sensitivity_data$HUC12) %>%
      arrange(HUC12)

    # Refit sensitivity model using exactly these HUC12s
    x <- sensitivity_data %>%
      select(all_of(vars))

    x_scaled <- scale(x)

    set.seed(123)

    km_sens <- kmeans(
      x_scaled,
      centers = k_primary,
      nstart = 100
    )

    tibble(
      variable_set = model_name,
      n_HUC12_compared = nrow(sensitivity_data),
      ARI_vs_primary =
        adjustedRandIndex(
          primary_data$primary_cluster,
          km_sens$cluster
        )
    )
  }
)

print(variable_set_ARI)

write.csv(
  variable_set_ARI,
  "../data/tidy/archetype_variable_set_ARI.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r pca_sens_analysis, dependson="planning_clusters"}
# ============================================================
# PCA-SCORE SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 20. Cluster on PCA scores as a sensitivity analysis
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# This directly addresses an important methodological question:
#
# Does the classification change substantially if highly
# correlated original variables are first reduced to a smaller
# number of principal components?
#
# The PRIMARY classification remains based on the standardized
# original variables.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Determine number of PCs explaining at least 90% of variance

n_pc_90 <- which(
  pca_variance$cumulative_percent >= 90
)[1]

cat(
  "\nNumber of PCs explaining >=90% of variance:",
  n_pc_90,
  "\n"
)


pca_scores_90 <- pca_model$x[, seq_len(n_pc_90), drop = FALSE]

set.seed(123)

km_pca <- kmeans(
  pca_scores_90,
  centers = k_primary,
  nstart = 100
)

pca_silhouette <- silhouette(
  km_pca$cluster,
  dist(pca_scores_90)
)

pca_sensitivity_summary <- tibble(
  model = paste0(
    "PCA scores (",
    n_pc_90,
    " PCs)"
  ),
  n_PC = n_pc_90,
  variance_explained =
    pca_variance$cumulative_percent[n_pc_90],
  mean_silhouette =
    mean(pca_silhouette[, "sil_width"]),
  median_silhouette =
    median(pca_silhouette[, "sil_width"]),
  min_silhouette =
    min(pca_silhouette[, "sil_width"])
)

print(pca_sensitivity_summary)


# Compare PCA solution with primary solution

pca_primary_ARI <- adjustedRandIndex(
  km_model$cluster,
  km_pca$cluster
)

cat(
  "\nAdjusted Rand Index: primary vs PCA-score solution =",
  round(pca_primary_ARI, 3),
  "\n"
)


write.csv(
  pca_sensitivity_summary,
  "../data/tidy/pca_cluster_sensitivity.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r treatment_performance, dependson="planning_clusters"}
# ============================================================
# TREATMENT-PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
# ============================================================
#
# These metrics answer a different question from the landscape
# classification: how do outcomes and implementation intensity
# compare per hectare actually treated?
# ============================================================

# ============================================================

cluster_summary <- huc12_planning %>%
  filter(!is.na(cluster)) %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(

    n = n(),

    # Landscape transformation
    mean_per_treated =
      mean(per_treated, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Practice configuration
    mean_per_patch =
      mean(per_patch, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_per_lin =
      mean(per_lin, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_per_rye =
      mean(per_rye, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Landscape-scale outcomes
    mean_no3_ha =
      mean(no3_ha, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_sed_ha =
      mean(sed_ha, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_ghg_ha =
      mean(ghg_ha, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_bio_Mg_ha =
      mean(bio_Mg_ha, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Direct implementation cost
    mean_dccp_ha =
      mean(dccp_ha, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Opportunity cost -- CHARACTERIZATION ONLY
    mean_oc_ha =
      mean(oc_ha, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Total cost -- CHARACTERIZATION ONLY
    mean_tccp_ha =
      mean(tccp_ha, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Treatment-level outcomes
    no3_treated = mean(no3_per_treated_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    sed_treated = mean(sed_per_treated_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    ghg_treated = mean(ghg_per_treated_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    bio_treated = mean(bio_per_treated_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    per_treated =  mean(per_treated, na.rm = TRUE),
    rye_treated =  mean(rye_share_treated, na.rm = TRUE),

    dccp_treated = mean(dccp_per_treated_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    oc_treated = mean(oc_per_treated_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    tccp_treated = mean(tccp_per_treated_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    

    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
